new_candidates.body:
Goal: the force an SPH liquid puts on a coupled body (rigid or FEM) must be (1) balanced, meaning the body takes
exactly the opposite of what the liquid takes, and (2) statically exact, meaning a body at rest in a liquid at rest
gets rho g V_submerged.

All numbers below come from WCSPH on CPU in fp64, averaged over steps 50-99 unless noted.

Test bodies:
- Fixed raft, 0.1 x 0.1 x 0.04 m (A = 0.01 m^2), in a 0.3-0.4 m pool.
- Fixed cube, 0.1 m.
- Floating FEM cube, 0.1 m, rho 500.

"Expected" uses the free-surface level measured away from the body. That level carries about half a particle size of
uncertainty, which matters for the flush and floating cases. Fully submerged cases don't depend on it.

## Forms tried

| # | Form | Balanced | Raft, submerged (expected 3.92 N) | Cube, submerged (expected 9.81 N) | Floating FEM cube draft (expected 0.05 m) |
|---|------|----------|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| 0 | Pair form, single ghost layer, column-hydrostatic ghost pressure (#3763 as merged) | yes, by construction | 5.85 N (+49%), 5.61 N (+43%) | not measured | 0.0468 m |
| 1 | A: body force = -sum p_s A_s n_s (Shepard-averaged surface pressure); liquid side as form 0 | no (see below) | 4.02 N (+2.5%), 4.11 N (+4.7%) | not measured | 0.0391 m |
| 2 | A + mirrored ghost pressure on the liquid side (p_g = p_i + rho0 g . (x_g - x_i)) | no: the body gets about 1.1 N (22% of its weight) less than the liquid, sign tied to the heave phase | same as form 1 | not measured | 0.0558 m, heave fails the 0.1 m/s rest bound |
| 3 | A + Shepard redistribution of each sample's opposite impulse to the particles | yes, by construction | 6.41 N (+64%), 6.86 N (+75%) | not measured | 0.0323 m; liquid penetrates the body |
| 4 | Pair form + mirroring + per-particle corrected gradient (L_i renormalization), offline | yes | 2.92 N (-26%), 5.17 N (+32%) | not measured | not measured |
| 5 | Pair form + mirroring + per-particle completeness rescaling of ghost terms, offline | yes | 7.86 N, 5.13 N | not measured | not measured |
| 6 | Pair form + mirroring + multi-layer ghosts (0.5 ps and 1.5 ps, clipped at the body midline) | yes | 5.33 N (+36%), 5.13 N (+31%) | 11.65 N (+19%), 11.56 N (+18%) | not measured |
| 7 | form 6 + normal-only hydrostatic extrapolation g . (n n^T) r, bodies only | yes | 5.91 N (+51%), 5.48 N (+40%) | 12.64 N (+29%) | not measured |

Not tried: B, the Band-style pressure boundary (symmetric pair on a Shepard p_b). It was evaluated offline and is
worse than form 0: +92% flush, +45% submerged.

Region split for the cube submerged at 0.18:
- form 6: inner bottom face 6.58 N (expected 7.93 N, -17%); inner top face -2.54 N (expected -3.12 N, -19%); edges and side faces +7.51 N (about +2.5 N more than the hydrostatic share of their top and bottom parts).
- form 7: inner bottom 6.69 N, inner top -2.61 N, rest +8.56 N.

## What is established

1. The particle pressure field next to a body is close to hydrostatic, with two exceptions.
   - Under a floating body, the column-hydrostatic wall model under-supports the first layer, because its column ends at the body. The liquid then over-compresses locally: +434 Pa in the first layer. Mirroring (form 2, form 6) removes this.
   - WCSPH carries a uniform compression offset of +30 to +60 Pa (+100 Pa in the surface layer). It is not yet compared to the equation-of-state compressibility.
   - The first-layer density equals the far-field density at the same depth to 0.1 kg/m^3.
2. A (surface pressure integral) is statically right within about 5%, because it uses the pressure at the surface directly. It is not balanced against any liquid-side force tried. A balanced redistribution (form 3) loses the near-field repulsion that keeps the liquid out of the body.
3. Every balanced pair form overshoots the static force.
   - The hydrostatic extrapolation is applied identically on both sides, so it is not a sign or reference error.
   - The overshoot is the pair operator itself: sum_i sum_g V_i V_g gradW does not reproduce the half-space plane-integral identity next to a finite body.
   - With a single ghost layer, the deeper liquid layers are over-completed (completeness scale 0.63-0.93).
   - With layers down to the support radius (form 6), the inner faces become under-pushed by about 18%, while edges and side faces carry a spurious vertical force.
4. The spurious vertical force on side faces comes from the hydrostatic part of the ghost pressure. A particle next to a vertical face is partly held up by the ghosts' vertical pressure gradient, so the face carries some of the liquid's weight. On the domain walls this is invisible, since walls take no force. Restricting the extrapolation to the normal direction (form 7) did not remove it: the rest region grew from 7.5 N to 8.6 N, and its source remains unexplained.
5. Corrections applied per particle (form 4, form 5) do not fix the body integral. They act on each particle's operator, while the body force is a sum over the particle-ghost pairs, and near a free surface completeness is undefined.

## Open questions

- The about 18% under-push on the inner faces with multi-layer ghosts (form 6): there is no explanation yet. Candidates are the layer volume at depth (area times ps, uncorrected for the layer's position) and the clipping near edges.
- The vertical force on side faces in form 6 and form 7: neither the full nor the normal-only hydrostatic term explains it. The next diagnostic would be the per-ghost force decomposition on a vertical face of an infinite slab (no edges).
- DFSPH: the stored p is the pressure the solve applied (warm start plus iterations). It reads 20-35% over hydrostatic in a settling pool. No settled-pool check yet.

## Directions for a decision

1. Use A for the body force, statically within about 5%, and accept that it is unbalanced (form 2: about 22% momentum imbalance, heave). This was ruled out by the balance requirement.
2. Hybrid with a defined split: the pair form gives the near-field repulsion, equal and opposite, and its static error is corrected by an equal-and-opposite pressure-integral term built from the same p_s. That is two mechanisms, which was ruled out.
3. Research a consistent boundary integral for finite bodies, for example a boundary-integral SPH formulation such as the semi-analytical wall boundaries of Ferrand et al., which computes the kernel's missing volume and gradient analytically against the true surface instead of with ghosts. It is balanced and consistent by construction, but it is a larger rework of the boundary model, including the domain walls.
4. Ship rigid-SPH on the pair form (form 0 or 6) with the static bias documented. The user ruled this out.

State of the rigid-SPH coupling branch (#3769, not merged, waiting on a validated boundary model): the pair form with mirroring and multi-layer ghosts (form 6), plus:
- the wet-gated added mass (with its FIXME);
- per-environment ghost activity and liquid removal for heterogeneous entities;
- domain-clipped sampling of fixed non-plane geoms (terrain);
- the coupler option and rigid material doc fixes;
- the empty-rigid-geom dtype fix;
- the ghost-sum fusion into the placement kernel;
- the floating-raft draft case in the flotation test.

## Engine prototypes of the semi-analytical boundary

Both prototypes compute gamma and grad gamma every substep by 7-point quadrature on the true surface segments. The
quadrature matches the analytic plane integral to 2.5e-4 of sigma(0). In both, the body takes the exact pairwise
opposite of the liquid's boundary force, and the in-kernel balance sum closes to about 1e-15 relative in every run.

| # | Form | Non-penetration | Static force |
|---|------|-----------------|--------------|
| 8 | Ferrand: summation density renormalized by gamma, boundary term over grad gamma with p_s | fails: particles enter the cube (negative deficit = inside); 4 of 6 runs blow up | raft flush -22%, cube 0.18 +15% (the only stable runs, not meaningful) |
| 9 | Density maps: rho = (sum V W + (1 - gamma)) rho0, boundary term rho0 (p_a/rho_a^2 + p_s/rho0^2) grad gamma | fails: by step 5 a particle sits 3 mm inside the cube moving at 0.5-1 m/s with density 1000; 2 particles inside | not measured (gate stops at non-penetration) |

Why both fail on non-penetration with this WCSPH (summation density, equation of state clamped at rho >= rho0):
- A single particle approaching a wall loses its neighbors at the rate it gains boundary volume, so its density stays
  near rho0 and its pressure is zero.
- The ghost pair forms resisted through the steep W(r) of a close ghost. gamma adds only a smooth integral, about 0.5
  at the surface.
- Ferrand relies on the continuity-equation density; density maps rely on DFSPH-strength incompressibility.
| 10 | Density maps (form 9) + a no-penetration velocity constraint (combined normal of the segments within half a particle size, approaching relative velocity only, opposite impulse to the segments) | passes: the deficit stays >= 0 over 100 steps; standoff 0.0094-0.0098 m | cube: flush +7.5%, 0.13 +19.8%, 0.17 +11.8%; the inner bottom face is over-pushed by 15-18%; the constraint still applies up to 2.9 N at rest |
new_candidates.title: [Feature]: Make the force of SPH liquids on moving bodies exact at rest
